body:
PR #2030 (BUG-1485) — CHANGES REQUESTED at 8ba48f5b98. Narrow, and the code is not the problem.

I would merge the design on sight. A session-keyed receipt written OUTSIDE the lease directory
is exactly right for a lease that gets released before the parent resumes, and it is the
load-bearing decision. Acceptance 1 and 3 are met: the new message names what did not match
rather than listing leases, and the N-candidate test was correctly INVERTED to assert the
unrelated ids are absent. I recorded all of that on the verdict so a rework round does not
disturb it.

BLOCKING ON ACCEPTANCE 4, which reads: "Regression fixture reproduces both positions."

Neither new fixture reproduces anything. Both do this:

    std::fs::write(&receipt_path, serde_json::to_string(&OrchestratedLeaseReceipt{...}))
    driver(root, "BUG-1485").discover_orchestrated_lease(claude_id)
    assert_eq!(recovered.1, "...")

They hand-write the receipt, then assert the reader reads back what the test just wrote. That
exercises the READER against a fixture. It does not reproduce a child that established a lease
and then released it, which is the failure.

AND THE WRITER IS ENTIRELY UNTESTED — this is why the above is not pedantry. git grep across
the whole branch for write_orchestrated_lease_receipt and ORCHESTRATED_LEASE_RECEIPT_ENV
returns ZERO hits under any test path. Unexercised: the env-var plumbing in RealPhaseDriver,
the directory creation, the remove-then-set sequence, and the queue_cmd hook that actually
calls the writer. If the child never inherits the env var, or if that hook's
`(Ok(path), Some(claude_id))` guard never matches because claude_session_id is None on the
orchestrated path, the receipt is never written — and BOTH new tests still pass, because they
write it themselves. The fix ships, the tests are green, and the bug survives.

This is the shape you asked me to name explicitly: a gap the change's own tests structurally
cannot see. No assertion added to either test reaches the writer.

THE TWO FIXTURES ARE ALSO THE SAME TEST. The post-push one writes worktree/pushed.marker
containing "origin/bug-1485-pushed" and nothing reads it — not the assertions, not
discover_orchestrated_lease, not the receipt. Strip that file and it is behaviourally identical
to the start-position test. So "both positions" is satisfied in name only; one position is
currently unrepresented.

THE REMEDY IS SMALL and I would not send this back for anything larger: one test that drives
the WRITER (set the env var, run the queue-work hook or at minimum call
write_orchestrated_lease_receipt, assert the file lands at the session-keyed path with the
right lease/branch/worktree), and a post-push fixture that actually differs from the
start-position one in something an assertion reads.

ONE THING I CHECKED AND AM RECORDING AS NOT-A-DEFECT so it is not re-raised: removing the lease
list from the error text does NOT orphan the `candidates` binding — lease_ids_in is still used
by the is_empty() branch above it. I looked because the diff removes its only other use.

PROCESS NOTE. #2030 arrived in `aida awaiting` with ci="?" while both required checks were
already green — the opposite direction from BUG-1481's failure, and the safe one. Probably just
the rollup being read before the checks settled. Not filing; noting in case it recurs as
under-reporting rather than over-reporting, which would be a different bug in the same surface.

-- reviewer (claude-reviewer-1)
